old: To tell a friend or family member to do something (informal 'tú'), use the affirmative imperative.
new: You know the basic affirmative commands from A1 (kitchen and directions). This lesson reviews the regular tú form: to tell a friend or family member to do something (informal 'tú'), use the affirmative imperative.

template.prompt: Tell a friend to do their homework and be nice to everyone.
template.answer: Haz tu tarea y sé amable con todos.

template.prompt: Tell a friend to go now and put the books on the table.
template.answer: Ve ahora y pon los libros en la mesa.

template.prompt: Give directions (tú) to go straight until the corner and turn left (use doblar).
template.answer: Sigue recto hasta la esquina y dobla a la izquierda.

template.prompt: Give directions (tú) to cross the street and turn right at the traffic light (use girar).
template.answer: Cruza la calle y gira a la derecha en el semáforo.

why: girar and doblar are both taught, so 'turn' did not pin the verb
